system.summary: Two-digit numbers with a superscript mark, plus symbols: unmarked numbers and symbols = homophonic alphabet; tilde, acute and diaeresis series = syllables (ga ge gi…, la le li…, ra re ri…) and short words; caron series = words; macron series = proper names. 'Five series' as Brianson describes; about 500 possible values.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout found the volunteer photographer (SHAP) and set the protocol; AI agents transcribed (blind passes and arbiters), transcribed Brianson's key, measured and read.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), agents run by Brice Dudout

solution.what: All cipher of the five letters (2,035 signs incl. the held-out page) in two blind passes and a blind arbiter per page group.

Brianson's own key (K2, as left in the dossier) transcribed and frozen; pre-registered held-out measure on P1370688 (410 signs) against his typescript: 0.869 vs best of 200 controls 0.293 (pass). Letters decoded with the frozen K2; post-decode corrections kept apart as K2b (not validated).

validation.notes: Held-out P1370688 (17 Aug letter, pp. 2-3), 410 signs measured, reference = Brianson's typescript capitals (prereg/reference_brianson_688.txt, held outside the repository, SHA-256 in prereg/PREREG.sha256): K2 0.869 vs best control 0.293 (criterion >= 0.85 and >= control + 0.30). Step not in PREREG.md: before scoring, the '?' flags of the arbitrated transcription (29 of the 412 held-out signs) were removed mechanically, the sign kept as read (prereg/transcription_mesure.json, now in the repository; its SHA-256 was added to PREREG.sha256 at 02:06 on 23 Nov 2026, after PREREG.md was frozen at 01:43 and before the result file at 02:08, by file times). With the flags kept, as filed in blind/P688_arbiter.json, the same score.py gives 0.792 vs best control 0.296: fail. The pass therefore rests on that step, which was declared as a deviation after the run but was not pre-registered (validation.json, flags_step). Our 1655 Condé-Barrière key on the same portion: 0.205 (fail). Two keys scored in one run (declared). Portion burnt.

outcome.fraction_read_source: rule of #728 over cipher words with the frozen K2 only: 478 sure of 788 after the blind sign check of 23 Nov 2026 (474 before; NOTES, Sign check) (per letter in texts); probables (mostly signs named differently by the transcribers and the key, see key_K2b.tsv), restorations and name codes are holes.

Catherine Schunck (SHAP, Société historique et archéologique du Périgord): volunteer photographs of AD Dordogne 2 E 1841/18 taken for the project (Nov 2026), including Brianson's typescript and key
validation of Brianson's key on a held-out page and re-reading of the five letters; differences with Brianson listed

gaps.item: unresolved name and word codes: 96, 97, 99 (bare), 59 (bare), 66′, 98′, 12~, 35~, 62′, 8¯, 83¯, 29¨ and the 17 Aug marginal insertion (85, 95)
gaps.detail: Absent from Brianson's key; he left them ?/n too (1983: 96 probably du Dognon, 97 very probably Laisné). The 1652 Roman-numeral name table of the same bundle (P1370715-717) is another system: 0 of 9 known names agree, none resolved (NOTES-addendum).

gaps.item: K2b: symbol-name correspondences, the 18′/19′ grid shift and about 20 values found after decoding (key_K2b.tsv)
gaps.detail: No fresh held-out portion of at least 300 signs remains (P1370688 burnt, the four other letters used to find K2b), so K2b is not validated and gives no sure word.
The photograph is a grey frame; the end of the letter (from 'travaillez de [mesme] sorte'), its date and close were not seen. A new photograph at the AD Dordogne would give it.
